title: transcription-language.v1
description: The language a meeting bot transcribes in: the setting itself, where each tier of it is written (a meeting's spawn request and live change, a person's default, the deployment's default), and the setting a meeting is running with, and the languages a caller's bots can transcribe (`LanguageCatalog`, from `catalog.json`). One rule beyond the shapes, enforced by validate.mjs and by every runtime that reads these shapes: when both `language` and a non-empty `allowed_languages` are set, `language` is one of the list.

LanguageCode.description: A Whisper language code: two or three lower-case letters (`de`, `en`, `yue`).

LanguageList.description: The languages detection is restricted to. Empty means no restriction.

LanguageSetting.description: auto: neither field set — each window is detected freely. forced: `language` set, list empty — every window is pinned to it. restricted: list set — a window detected outside the list is transcribed again pinned to `language` (a member of the list) or, when it is null, to the first entry; a one-entry list pins to that entry.

Source.description: Which tier supplied a meeting's setting. Precedence, first tier that sets either field wins as a whole: meeting, then user, then history (the languages the person's recent meetings were spoken in, restricted to that list, set only when the person has no default), then deployment, then auto.

EffectiveSetting.description: The setting a meeting's bot runs with, stored on the meeting as `data.transcription_language` and returned on every meeting read. meeting-api is its one writer: at spawn, and on every accepted live change.

SpawnFields.description: The language fields of a `POST /bots` body (the rest of that body is api.v1's). Both absent or null: the meeting tier is unset and lower tiers apply. `language: "auto"` sets the meeting tier to auto, over any default.

ConfigUpdate.description: The body of `PUT /bots/{platform}/{native_meeting_id}/config`. It REPLACES the running setting: an omitted or null field is cleared, so `{"language": null, "allowed_languages": null}` is auto. At least one of the two is present.

task.description: Accepted for the api.v1 shape and carried to the bot unchanged.

ConfigAccepted.description: The 202 answer to a live change: the change was delivered to the running bot and is now the meeting's setting.

UserPreferenceUpdate.description: The language fields of `PUT /user/transcription` (the person's default). `""` clears `language`; `[]` clears the list; an absent field is unchanged.

UserPreference.description: The language fields of `GET /user/transcription`, and of identity's internal bot-context answer under `transcription_language` (present there only when the person set either field).

DeploymentDefault.description: meeting-api's environment: `DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION_LANGUAGE` (a code, or empty) and `DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LANGUAGES` (comma-separated codes, or empty) — Helm `meetingApi.transcriptionLanguage` and `meetingApi.transcriptionAllowedLanguages`. meeting-api refuses to boot on a value this contract refuses.

CatalogLanguage.description: One language the caller's transcription model can transcribe: its code (the value `language` and `allowed_languages` take) and its English name, both from `catalog.json`.

CatalogSource.description: How the list was chosen. provider: the transcription backend named its model (`GET {url}/health` → `model`) and `catalog.json` lists that model. configured: the model id configured for the caller's backend (Settings, else `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL`) is listed there. assumed: no model is known, or the known one is not listed, so the list is every code the language fields accept.

LanguageCatalog.description: The answer to `GET /transcription/languages`: the languages a bot this caller sends can transcribe, and the deployment's default setting (`DeploymentDefault` as a setting; auto when unset). The default is the lowest tier, not a limit: a meeting, a person's default and their history all override it, with any code in `languages`. Beyond the shape, enforced by validate.mjs and by meeting-api's tests: `languages` is exactly the `catalog.json` list for `model` (every code, in catalog order, under its catalog name) — the full list when `source` is assumed — and `model` is set unless `source` is assumed.

model.description: The model id the list was chosen for, as the backend or the configuration names it; null when none is known.

ModelLookup.description: A golden-only shape pinning how `catalog.json` reads one model id: how many codes it lists (null: the id is not listed), and codes the list must and must not hold.

x-routes.auth: the caller's key (scope `bot`); the effective setting is stored on the new meeting as data.transcription_language and carried to the bot as invocation.v1 `language` + `allowedLanguages`. Refusals: 422 a body this contract refuses

the caller's key (scope `bot`); allowed for the meeting's owner and for an owner or contributor of the workspace the meeting is bound to. Delivered as an acts.v1 `reconfigure` on bot_commands:meeting:{meeting_id}. Refusals: 403 neither owner nor editor, 404 no active bot the caller can see, 409 the bot is not listening yet (nothing changed), 422 a body this contract refuses, 503 the caller's workspace role could not be read
the caller's own account (identity admin-api). Refusals: 422 a body this contract refuses

the caller's key (scope `bot` or `tx`). The list is for the backend this caller's bots transcribe with: their Settings backend, else the deployment's. Only a backend the deployment owns is asked for its model; a customer's own endpoint is never called from here, and its configured model id decides. The backend's answer is cached for 5 minutes; an unreachable backend, or one that names no model, falls to the next source. No refusals beyond the edge's (401, 403)
